question: What was the primary explanation for mental illness during the demonological era?
explanation: Early societies attributed mental health struggles to supernatural causes rather than biological diseases. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why was trephining performed on individuals exhibiting severe behavioral disturbances in ancient times?

options.B: To relieve elevated intracranial pressure from trauma
options.C: To allow trapped evil spirits to escape

explanation: Boring holes into the skull was believed to release the demons causing the madness. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h1)

question: What was the primary outcome of establishing early psychiatric asylums?

options.B: Rapid healing through specialized medical therapies
options.C: Overcrowding and inhumane warehousing of patients

explanation: Asylums quickly deteriorated into overcrowded, brutal holding facilities instead of therapeutic sanctuaries. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h2)

question: A patient in a historical asylum was most likely to experience which environmental condition?

options.B: Heavy physical restraints and poor sanitation
options.C: Nutritious diets and cheerful recovery wards

explanation: Early institutions lacked modern therapeutics and relied heavily on mechanical restraints and neglect. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h2)

question: Who was the French pioneer famous for unchaining patients and championing moral treatment?
explanation: Philippe Pinel led the humanitarian movement in France by removing physical restraints from asylum inmates. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h3)

question: What was the core philosophy behind the moral treatment movement in psychiatry?

options.A: Isolation is necessary to protect the general public
options.B: Spiritual exorcism remains the best intervention
options.C: Compassionate care and a peaceful environment heal the mind
options.D: Strict chemical sedation cures psychiatric disorders

explanation: Moral treatment emphasized respect, kindness, and purposeful activity over chains and punishment. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h3)

question: Who is historically celebrated as America's first trained nurse and a pioneer in psychiatric nursing?
explanation: Linda Richards graduated in 1873 and spearheaded the formal training of nurses for psychiatric facilities. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why was the establishment of training schools by Linda Richards a major milestone for mental health?

options.A: It allowed psychiatric nurses to prescribe medications independently
options.B: It closed down all large state-run mental institutions
options.C: It eliminated the need for medical doctors in asylums
options.D: It transformed asylum guards into skilled therapeutic caregivers

explanation: Formal education shifted the role from passive custodianship to active, educated nursing intervention. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which medication introduced in the 1950s revolutionized the treatment of severe psychiatric conditions?
explanation: Chlorpromazine was the pioneering antipsychotic drug that transformed inpatient psychiatric management. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h5)

question: How did the arrival of psychotropic drugs alter the daily routine of inpatient psychiatric units?

options.A: It made nursing assessments entirely unnecessary
options.B: It increased the need for permanent mechanical restraints
options.C: It decreased violent behaviors and shortened hospital stays
options.D: It caused patients to become permanently unresponsive

explanation: Controlling acute symptoms chemically allowed patients to stabilize faster and leave the hospital sooner. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h5)

question: What major global movement occurred in psychiatry during the 1960s and 1970s?
explanation: Deinstitutionalization involved discharging patients from large asylums into community-based settings. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h6)

question: What unintended problem arose immediately following the mass closure of large psychiatric asylums?

options.A: An immediate shortage of nursing school applicants
options.B: Excessive funding surpluses in local health clinics
options.C: A complete global eradication of mental illness
options.D: Homelessness and lack of local community support systems

explanation: Without adequate local infrastructure, many discharged patients faced severe neglect and homelessness. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which facility is recognized as the first formal institution for mental health care in Nigeria?
explanation: Established in Lagos in 1907, Yaba Lunatic Asylum began formal institutional psychiatric care in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h7)

question: What was the unique significance of the Aro Village system developed by T. Adeoye Lambo?

options.A: It completely banned the use of modern psychotropic medications
options.B: It relied exclusively on European medical expatriates for staffing
options.C: It locked all psychiatric patients inside high-security fortress walls
options.D: It integrated local community culture and families into patient treatment

explanation: Lambo's village model respected local culture by housing patients within supportive host families. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h7)

question: Modern psychiatric nursing practice places primary emphasis on which of the following approaches?

options.C: Sole reliance on spiritual exorcism rituals
options.D: Strict custodial guarding behind locked doors

explanation: Contemporary psychiatric nursing focuses on comprehensive recovery, therapeutic communication, and patient rights. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h8)

question: Why is the advocacy role of the psychiatric nurse vital in contemporary clinical practice?

options.A: To restrict patient family members from visiting wards
options.B: To replace hospital administrators in financial budgeting
options.C: To actively combat social stigma and protect patient rights
options.D: To avoid administering prescribed psychiatric medications

explanation: Nurses advocate for vulnerable patients to ensure dignity, equity, and freedom from discrimination. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h8)
